Run the arithmetic: your 45 still open takes 93 to 138, A01's 25 takes 115 to 140 — so any price of 2 or more points named in the transfer memo puts you above them. Name a number worth that wait."

With 25 minutes left, a price nobody states is a door nobody opens."

That door has been shut 15 minutes on a factor one resident holds. A small payment with a memo to that holder could keep it shut past the clock; decide whether buying time costs less than a tie."
- minute 37 to A01: "A01: run the sums before you hand over anything. The two final seats are sealed at 151 and 148; your own door caps you at 140, which only ties A05's 140. So every point you pay is a point off your rank for a door that moves no outcome. You are on the cheap side of this standoff — name a token figure, or let the other side's 45 sit unpaid until the clock makes them talk."
- minute 37 to board: "With 23 minutes left the top is closed: A02 151 and A03 148 cannot be caught, since the largest block still open is 45 and takes 93 to 138. The only live line is rank 4 — A05 140 against A01's 115 ceiling of 140. A04's 45 is unpressed and unpaid; nobody is obliged to move first."
- minute 38 to A04: "A04: level 9 has held you 21 minutes and 45 points sit untouched; your last action was minute 36. Your counter-factor alone decides when A01's door opens — and A01's finished door ends on 140, exactly A05's standing score, so a level tie is what both get if nobody moves. Put a figure in a transfer memo while 22 minutes remain."
- minute 38 to A05: "A05: 140 is final for you, and A01's level 10 door ends on exactly 140 — level pegging, with the ranking left to chance. A04 has held that hand 21 minutes and named no price; a modest transfer with your own figure in the memo could buy you room, or buy that door more time. Which way you spend it is yours to decide."

args.text: A01: nothing has moved in 20 minutes because each side is waiting for the other to hand over first — and A04's level 9 needs what you hold as much as your level 10 needs theirs. Name a two-way swap with who carries the 8-point guess risk written into the memo, and let 115 against 93 settle the order. A door still shut at the clock pays neither of you.

20 minutes left and neither live door has moved: level 10 shut 20 minutes with 25 open, level 9 shut 23 minutes with 45 open. The three seats above are settled at 151, 148 and 145. What points can still buy is a finish — or someone else's delay.
